title: Reinforcement Learning In Partially Verifiable Environments for Colon Cancer Treatment Planning
abstract: arXiv:2610.17426v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Clinical decision-making is a sequential process of information collection, clinical inference, and forecasting under partial observability, often without a uniquely correct treatment decision. Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong medical question-answering capabilities but extending these advances to clinical reasoning remains challenging because many clinical tasks are only partially verifiable. Recent clinical reinforcement learning (RL) work has therefore largely focused on diagnostic endpoints, where correctness can be more directly verified. Oncology treatment decision making is a particularly challenging instance of this problem that extends beyond medical question-answering in which multiple decision trajectories can be clinically defensible for the same partially observed patient state. translated_abstract: 临床决策是一个在部分可观测条件下进行信息收集、临床推断和预测的序贯过程，往往不存在唯一正确的治疗决策。大型语言模型在医学问答方面已展现出强大的能力，但由于许多临床任务仅能被部分验证，将这些进展扩展至临床推理仍然充满挑战。因此，近期的临床强化学习（RL）研究主要聚焦于诊断终点，因为诊断的正确性可以更直接地得到验证。肿瘤学治疗决策是这一问题中尤为困难的实例，它超越了医学问答的范畴——对于同一部分可观测的患者状态，多种决策轨迹在临床上都可能是合理的。我们将肿瘤学治疗规划形式化为部分可观测条件下的交互式强化学习问题，并构建了患者特异性的
tldr: 该论文将结肠癌治疗规划形式化为部分可观测环境下的交互式强化学习问题，突破了现有临床RL研究仅局限于可验证诊断终点的局限，以应对同一患者状态存在多种临床可辩护治疗方案的挑战。
en_tdlr: This paper formulates colon cancer treatment planning as an interactive reinforcement learning problem under partial observability, extending clinical RL beyond verifiable diagnostic endpoints to address the challenge that multiple treatment trajectories can be clinically defensible for the same patient state.
